supplier_power.rationale: Korea shipped US$0.59bn FOB of 'body cleansing products' in 2025 (HIGH, MFDS via Yonhap/Korea Herald) — the third-largest of the four segment export values on file, behind skincare (US$8.54bn) and colour cosmetics (US$1.51bn) and far ahead of fragrances (US$0.06bn), all same year and same EXPORT_FOB basis. An export flow of that size evidences scaled, export-qualified production capacity standing behind the category rather than a boutique make. Against that, Korea's brand owners have three listed contract manufacturers to choose from (Cosmax, Kolmar Korea, Cosmecca Korea) plus in-house capacity at LG H&H, so no single maker holds pricing leverage over a brand owner. This is an inference from the export flow and the ODM roster — there is no bath-specific supplier, cost or margin DataPoint — hence THIN.

overall.rationale: Export-visible, domestically unmeasured. The US$0.59bn 2025 export flow is a genuine, HIGH-confidence signal that Korea has scaled body-cleansing manufacturing and international demand for it — enough to rate supplier power LOW and to make the category interesting as a sourcing base. It says nothing about the Korean home market, which has no size, growth or share data at all, so no attractiveness call for a domestic-share entrant is defensible. Note the export figure is the customs 'body cleansing products' category and must not be read as domestic retail.
